reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). Verdict: revise, because of two major findings. I checked the plan against the snapshot with Read and Grep only; I ran nothing. The functions, seams and helpers the plan names all exist, and the change sits where each fault starts: target/produce is deleted after the checks pass and before the pre-verifier gate (run/mod.rs:2178), and kept when a check fails. Making timeout_seed aware of the resume stage is the right fix for the retry. The first major finding: the criterion 6 test cannot pass even with the fix. Its reader reports 9.5 GB as soon as target/produce exists, so the job stops at the disk gate before the checks (line 1980), before the removal runs. The second: the plan drops the interrupted-process cause, which the request and criterion 3 both require, though interrupted jobs are already recognised and their invocation records recovered. The minor findings: the reader still runs on athena retry and the test should say so; is_environment_reason should be reused rather than a near-duplicate added; and the criterion 2 test should use a marker file instead of counting reads. Findings: major: The criterion 6 test stops at the disk gate before the checks, so it fails even with the fix. (Demonstrations, Criterion 6 (nine_and_a_half_gb_free); run/mod.rs:1980 (disk gate before the checks)); major: The plan drops the 'interrupted process' cause, which the request and criterion 3 both require. (Risks (interrupted process); Open questions 2; criterion 3); minor: The retry still runs the reader agent, and neither the plan nor its test says so. (Demonstrations, Criterion 2; reading.rs:833-846); minor: is_resumable_stop nearly duplicates the existing disk::is_environment_reason. (Decision 4 / Step 1; disk.rs:203); minor: Counting reads of the free-space function in the criterion 2 test is fragile. (Demonstrations, Criterion 2)
